newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-JONES HOLDS FIVE-STROKE LEAD AT PHOENIX OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JONES HOLDS FIVE-STROKE LEAD AT PHOENIX OPEN.

text.p: Steve Jones set no more records Saturday but his six-under-par 65 was enough to hold his five-stroke lead after the third round of the Phoenix Open and put him in position to match or break the PGA Tour's all-time scoring record.
If Jones, who is now 22 under par, shoots five under on Sunday he will equal the 72-hole scoring record of 27 under set by Ben Hogan in 1945.

Jones, whose 16-under 126 total after two rounds had equalled the best 36-hole start in PGA history, goes into Sunday's round five strokes in front of David Duval, who also shot 65 to go to 17 under par.
In third place at 13 under par, nine behind Jones, were three players: Tommy Tolles (68), Rick Fehr (66) and Fulton Allem of South Africa (66).
Though he was not among the leaders, Tiger Woods caused much of the excitement at the Phoenix Open on Saturday.
On the rowdiest hole on the PGA Tour, the 6,000 capacity 16th hole at the TPC of Scottsdale, Woods sent a nine-iron hopping into the hole for the second ace of his brief professional career.
The noise it brought forth from the crowd may have been the loudest ever heard on a golf course.

"I've had some pretty good moments in my career, but that was right up there," said Woods. "It was without a doubt the loudest roar I've ever heard. I don't really remember what happened immediately afterward because I kind of went crazy myself. It was amazing, people were just going nuts."
Woods finished with a 67 to stand at 10 under par, 12 shots behind Jones. Woods would probably need a 59 on Sunday to catch him, a score he feels is within his means if perhaps not likely this week.

Jones started the third round strongly, with birdies on the first three holes, and finished off well, with birdies on three of the last four. In between there were two bogeys, bringing his week's total to three, and two more birdies.
"I have to play well tomorrow, no one is going to give this to me," Jones said. "I have to keep focussing in on birdies, because it would be a big disappointment to lose this tournament."
Should Jones win it would be the sixth win of his career, and his first since winning the U.S. Open last June at Oakland Hills.
